recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It preserves the already-correct Attachment.contentType source and fixes the remaining active narrative BCP-13 RFC Editor link with the stable URL named by FHIR-6183; do not expand this issue into the separate FHIR-36705 maxBinding cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-6183 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core DSTU1 correction asking that the broken BCP-13 link in the Attachment.contentType description stop using http://www.rfc-editor.org/bcp/bcp13.txt.html and use the RFC Editor BCP-13 reference instead; a reporter comment later identified http://www.rfc-editor.org/bcp/bcp13.txt as the apparent correct URL at that time.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-6183. Current Attachment source defines Attachment.contentType with the MimeType binding and no embedded BCP-13 hyperlink, and a source-wide search found no bcp13.txt.html URL remaining.
additional_context: The current terminology narrative still used http://www.rfc-editor.org/bcp/bcp13.txt for a Mime Types example link; that URL now returns 404, while https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp13 returns 200 and matches the stable target family requested in the issue. A 2022 Zulip thread tied the old rfc-editor.org/bcp/bcp13.txt value set reference to Attachment.contentType-era bindings and validator confusion, but its Expression maxBinding follow-up belongs to FHIR-36705.
reconciliation: Changed source/terminologies.html so the Mime Types example points to https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp13. No datatype, terminology, or conformance semantics changed.
source_changes: source/terminologies.html: updated the Mime Types BCP-13 example link from http://www.rfc-editor.org/bcp/bcp13.txt to https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp13.

related_jiras.note: The 2022 Zulip thread about http://www.rfc-editor.org/bcp/bcp13.txt not found ended with a separate Expression maxBinding Jira; it was useful context but was not re-decided for this Attachment/contentType link correction.
